chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us from his book in Safar of the year four and seventy (74) and two hundred (200), saying: Al-Abbas ibn Aamir ibn Rabah ath-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ar-Rabee' al-Aqra' narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said:
When as-Sufyani conquers the five districts, then count to him nine months. And Hisham claimed that the five districts were: Damascus, Palestine, Jordan, Hims and Halab.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: As-Sufyani, a key eschatological figure in Shia tradition who rises before the appearance of the Mahdi.
key_terms.الْكُورِ الْخَمْسِ: The five districts, referring to specific geographical regions in the Levant.
key_terms.تِسْعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ: Nine months, the specified duration of as-Sufyani's rule in these districts.

ai.seo_question: What are the five districts controlled by as-Sufyani and how long will his rule last?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'five districts' (Kour Khams) as Damascus, Palestine, Jordan, Homs, and Aleppo, establishing the geographical scope of the Sufyani's initial power base in the Levant. This nine-month period is interpreted by Shia scholars as a critical window of opportunity for the Mahdi's emergence, marking the transition from the Sufyani's tyranny to the global justice of the Awaited Imam.
